items.title: Celtics star Jayson Tatum called for technical after throwing ball toward official late in loss to Nuggets
items.summary: Jayson Tatum got called for a technical foul at the worst time on Wednesday night, and it cost the Boston Celtics a chance at extending the game. Tatum was called for a technical foul after he threw a ball toward an official in the final seconds of the Celtics' 105-101 loss to the Denver Nuggets at Ball Arena on Wednesday. While the act itself didn't cost the Celtics the game, it made sure they didn't have a legitimate chance to send the contest into overtime. Denver star Jamal Murray drained a jumper with just seven seconds left in the game, which put the Nuggets up by three points at the time. Tatum caught the ball after it went through the net, and started to make a move to pass it in as the Celtics called a timeout. items.title: Kawhi Leonard Dealing With Patellar Tendinopathy
items.summary: After being the team’s headlining off-season move, Kawhi Leonard has only played two games for the Raptors this season before being sidelined with what was described as left knee swelling. Now, the injury he is dealing with has been revealed to be patellar tendinopathy, Josh Lewenberg reports for TSN Sports (Twitter video link). That’s the same recurring condition that Leonard and Toronto were forced to manage in his previous stint with the Raptors in 2019, which required significant load management. The nature of the condition, which is a result of areas within the quadriceps tendon developing some level of degeneration, is such that it can only be effectively treated by reducing high-stress activity, Lewenberg notes. That has led the team to be more cautious when it comes to bringing him back early. The star forward is still progressing in his return to play and is targeting a return…

items.title: Players Eligible For In-Season Veteran Extensions In 2026/27
items.summary: As we explain in our glossary entry on veteran contract extensions, rookie scale extensions used to be the most common form of contract extension in the NBA. However, recent Collective Bargaining Agreements have loosened the rules on eligibility for veteran extensions and made them more financially advantageous, especially for players who don’t expect mega-deals. As a result, we’ve seen a substantial bump in veteran contract extensions in recent seasons. In every league year since 2021/22, at least 17 players have signed veteran extensions, including 20 in 2025/26. We’re not quite up to 17 yet in ’26/27, but there’s plenty of time for this season’s list to continue to grow, right up until June 30, 2027. items.summary: The Cavaliers continue to shuffle players in and out of their two-way contract slots, announcing today in a press release that they’ve signed swingman Zack Austin to a two-way deal. In order to make room for Austin, Cleveland placed forward Riley Minix on waivers. Austin, 25, is a 6’5″ wing who went undrafted out of Pitt in 2025. He was in camp with the Thunder in 2025 before spending his rookie year with their G League affiliate, the Oklahoma City Blue. In 20 games for the Blue, he averaged 12.9 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 2.2 blocks in 27.4 minutes per contest. Those block numbers weren’t an anomaly for Austin, who averaged 1.8 BPG during his college career and led the ACC in blocked shots as a senior.
